original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-section}
Let $f : V \to U$ be a morphism of simplicial sets. Let $n \geq 0$ be an
integer. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item The map $f_i : V_i \to U_i$ is a bijection for $i < n$.
\item The map $f_n : V_n \to U_n$ is a surjection.
\item The canonical morphism $U \to \text{cosk}_n \text{sk}_n U$
is an isomorphism.
\item The canonical morphism $V \to \text{cosk}_n \text{sk}_n V$
is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}
Then $f$ is a trivial Kan fibration.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-homotopy}
Let $f^0, f^1 : V \to U$ be maps of simplicial sets.
Let $n \geq 0$ be an integer.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item The maps $f^j_i : V_i \to U_i$, $j = 0, 1$ are equal for $i < n$.
\item The canonical morphism $U \to \text{cosk}_n \text{sk}_n U$
is an isomorphism.
\item The canonical morphism $V \to \text{cosk}_n \text{sk}_n V$
is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}
Then $f^0$ is homotopic to $f^1$.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cosk-minus-one-equivalence}
Let $A$, $B$ be sets, and that $f : A \to B$ is a map. Consider the simplicial
set $U$ with $n$-simplices
$$
A \times_B A \times_B \ldots \times_B A\ (n + 1 \text{ factors)}.
$$
see Example \ref{example-fibre-products-simplicial-object}.
If $f$ is surjective, the morphism $U \to B$
where $B$ indicates the constant simplicial set with value $B$
is a trivial Kan fibration.

final_content.statement:
For any map of sets \(f:A\to B\), let \(U\) be its Čech nerve, with \(U_n=A\times_B\cdots\times_B A\) (\(n+1\) copies), faces dropping and degeneracies repeating factors.
Let $A$, $B$ be sets, and that $f : A \to B$ is a map. Consider the simplicial
set $U$ with $n$-simplices
$$
A \times_B A \times_B \ldots \times_B A\ (n + 1 \text{ factors)}.
$$
with faces induced by projections and degeneracies by diagonals.
If $f$ is surjective, the morphism $U \to B$
where $B$ indicates the constant simplicial set with value $B$
is a trivial Kan fibration.
hypotheses: Let f:A→B be a surjective map of sets, and U its Čech-nerve simplicial set with U_n=A^{×_B(n+1)}.
conclusions: The canonical augmentation U→constant(B) is a trivial Kan fibration.

semantic_review_note: The source's Čech nerve of a surjective map A→B has n-simplices (n+1)-fold B-fiber products with face projections and degeneracy diagonals. Its map to constant B is a trivial Kan fibration; expansion in the proposal is equivalent.
